It can be really confusing when a child invents elaborate and unusual stories like this. Children and adolescents sometimes make up bizarre tales for a variety of reasons. It could be a way to seek attention, test boundaries, or simply exercise a vivid imagination. Sometimes, creating shocking stories is a way for them to express underlying stress, complex emotions, or a desire for control, knowing it will get a reaction from you. 

To understand what is driving this, try asking her about the stories with gentle, non-judgmental curiosity rather than confronting the lie. You might ask where she got the idea or what she likes about the story. If this behavior is frequent, distressing, or accompanied by other changes in her mood or behavior, it could be very helpful to consult her pediatrician or a child mental health professional. They can help explore what might be going on beneath the surface and offer guidance on how to best support her.
